summary: Cleveland's unofficial 2026 depth chart lists Sampson as the clear RB2 behind Quinshon Judkins, with expectations of a real complementary role (projected around 800 combined yards) rather than token backup snaps.
Listed RB3 on Cleveland's depth chart behind Judkins and Dylan Sampson, projected as the early-down/goal-line complement in a crowded but real backfield rotation.
Appears on Cleveland's running back depth chart behind Judkins/Sampson/Sanders, but with no individual camp storyline reported beyond being named to the room — a 4th/5th-string longshot.

Reported to camp visibly leaner and has been turning heads through 2026 training camp, building a real case for the RB1 job over Aaron Jones as Minnesota leans into more wide-zone run concepts; the two are currently co-listed as starters on the team's first unofficial depth chart. His 2025 line (758 yards, 6 TDs, 4.8 ypc on 159 carries) may understate his 2026 role.

Second-year back whose sparse rookie 2025 (frequently inactive, small role) is a poor baseline for 2026: with Ameer Abdullah and Tyler Goodson both departing in free agency and Indianapolis using only a 7th-round pick (Seth McGowan) at the position, Giddens is set up as Jonathan Taylor's primary backup.

Traded from Jacksonville to Philadelphia for 2026 5th/6th-round picks after the Jaguars got crowded at RB (new HC Liam Coen, rookie Bhayshul Tuten). Lands as the Eagles' RB2 behind Saquon Barkley after incumbent backup Will Shipley suffered a rib injury. His 2025 Jacksonville role (58 carries, 344 yards, 2 TDs as a change-of-pace back) doesn't reflect this bigger opportunity.

4th on New Orleans' RB depth chart behind newly-signed Travis Etienne, Alvin Kamara, and (situationally) Kendre Miller/Devin Neal, but flashed real usage late in 2025 (35 carries, 157 yards over the final two games while others were hurt). Competing with Ty Chandler for a roster spot in a crowded, reshuffled backfield.

Re-signed with Tampa Bay after a career-best 2025 (320 rush yards, career-high 7 rushing TDs, team-leading 8 total TDs on 86 carries), but enters 2026 as RB3 behind Bucky Irving and newly-signed free agent Kenneth Gainwell (Rachaad White departed to Washington). His 2025 per-touch efficiency was real, but the touch share behind it is not guaranteed to repeat.

Finished 2025 strong (746 yards on 145 carries, 5.1 ypc, 6.9% explosive-run rate — 6th-best among 100+ carry backs) after a limited rookie year (58 carries). Multiple outlets project his 2026 workload growing significantly alongside Kyren Williams, potentially toward a real timeshare rather than a clear backup role.

With Trey Benson waived, Arizona's backfield is Jeremiyah Love/Tyler Allgeier/James Conner at the top, leaving Kiner competing with Bam Knight for a single potential 4th roster spot — a genuine longshot for the 53-man roster, not a lock.

Undrafted rookie (Pitt) was waived/injured by Buffalo on June 11, 2026 over an undisclosed issue and reverted to injured reserve; reporting indicates the team has moved on from him rather than planning a return. In real doubt for any 2026 role despite still showing on the roster.

Signed a modest one-year deal with Tennessee after reaching 600 scrimmage yards with Arizona in 2025, but the Titans' first unofficial 2026 depth chart has him behind Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears, rookie 5th-rounder Nick Singleton, and special-teamer Julius Chestnut — buried well below where his 2025 production alone would suggest.

Signed a 2-year, $10M free-agent deal with Jacksonville (replacing Travis Etienne, who left for New Orleans), made a full recovery from offseason foot surgery, and is listed as co-starter with 2nd-year back Bhayshul Tuten on the Jaguars' unofficial depth chart — head coach Liam Coen has said the touch split should be roughly equitable. His 2025 Washington line (500 yards, 6 TDs) undersells this new lead-role opportunity.

4th-round rookie (108th overall) competing for a rotational/3rd-down role behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey in Denver's backfield; scouted as a complete three-down back who fell in the draft mainly due to a lack of straight-line speed. Exact depth-chart order behind Dobbins is inconsistently reported across outlets as of late August.

Undrafted rookie (Ohio State, via West Virginia) power back competing for a short-yardage/goal-line roster spot in a very crowded New Orleans backfield (Etienne, Kamara, Neal, Miller, Estimé all ahead of him) — a longshot to make the 53-man roster.

Undrafted rookie (Tulsa, 1,065 rush yards in his final college season) was waived by Dallas in early August 2026 after the team signed Jashaun Corbin instead — he never played a regular-season snap for the Cowboys and is no longer on the roster despite being a projected practice-squad stash entering camp.
